claims.claim_ar: القراءة التفسيرية تُحوّل لفظ القِتَال (لِقِتَالٍ) إلى معنى اللقاء/المواجهة القتالية؛ استعمال مجازي/كنائي يربط لفظ القتال بمحض معنى اللقاء بالعدو.
claims.claim_en: The commentary states "al-liqa' (meeting) is commonly the name for combat", so the term قِتَال in the verse functions metonymically: it denotes the encounter/battle itself (a figurative/metonymic use).
claims.needs_review_reason: The source phrase explicitly defines 'اللقاء' as denoting combat; applying this as a metonymic reading of the verse's لِقِتَالٍ is plausible but is an interpretive step that should be checked against the immediate tafsir context for this specific verse.

claims.claim_ar: الآية تستعمل استثناءً مزدوجاً متوازيًا («إِلَّا مُتَحَرِّفًا لِقِتَالٍ أَوْ مُتَحَيِّزًا إِلَى فِئَةٍ») كأسلوب بلاغي موازي/مقابِل لتحديد استثناءات الهروب وتكثيف الإدانة.
claims.claim_en: The verse uses dual, parallel exception clauses ("except in turning away for fighting or in shifting to a faction") forming a parallel/antithetical rhetorical structure (tibaq). Tabari characterizes similar phrasing as "this is a forceful style of denial (جحود)", indicating the strong rhetorical effect of such parallel clauses.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source quote comments on forceful rhetorical style in a different passage; mapping that characterization onto the verse's paired exceptions is a plausible rhetorical reading but should be verified with dedicated rhetorical commentary on this ayah.
